newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - SAD year share seen up 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - SAD year share seen up 11 pct.

text.p: South African Druggists Ltd (SAD) is expected to report a rise in annual earnings, but at a much slower rate than last year due to a higher interest bill and a slowdown in consumer demand, analysts said on Friday.
The pharmaceutical and healthcare company is due to report results for the year to August 31 on Wednesday.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast attributable earnings rising to between 212 and 213 cents a share with a consensus of 212.5 from 191.4 a year ago.
This represented an increase of 11 percent compared to the 20 percent growth achieved in the 1994/95 year.
Analysts said they expected the dividend to climb to 69 cents a share from 62 cents a year ago.
"We had to downgrade our forecast as the financing side is up quite a bit," said Melanie da Costa, an analyst at Investec Securities.
"They put a lot of money into their medical side and it has not come to fruition," she said.
Analysts said SAD's volumes had slipped during the second half of the year amid a fall in demand as consumers became more cost conscious. This had resulted in margins being squeezed.
"Their volumes were not as positive in winter as they had hoped," said another analyst who asked not to be identified.
Da Costa said this was not specific to SAD, however, as conditions across the pharmaceutical and medical industry were tough.
SAD this week announced it had consolidated all its pharmaceutical businesses in a single company, Pharmacare Ltd, in a bid to make medicines more affordable.
But analysts remained sceptical of the benefits of the restructure. "It is an absolute non-event. They have done this before and I don't see it changing the prognosis for them," one said.
